clue.text: Horse following guns, probably just a trickle

indicators.note: the horse comes after the guns, so its word goes second

parts.note: a battery is a set of artillery guns
a charger is a cavalry horse

explanation.surface: A cavalry horse trails behind the artillery, but only a trickle of it seems to get through.
explanation.walkthrough: A trickle charger tops up a battery slowly, so the device is probably delivering just a trickle of current.
explanation.definitionFit: Many devices for topping up a car's cells work slowly, giving a small steady current called a trickle.

clue.text: A Tourist Trophy contest around junction getting d-drawn

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle race

indicators.note: the contest word is placed round the junction letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a race is a contest
a T-junction gives T
the stammered first letter of the word that follows supplies a D

explanation.surface: A motorbike race on a road with a T-junction draws a stammering crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'd-drawn' both supplies a lone D and leaves 'drawn' as the definition; T sits inside RACE between C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being attracted to something is being pulled or drawn towards it.

clue.text: The light in a light orchestra

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Asks what the light is in a light orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable lamp, a source of illumination.

clue.text: Not lying down for a breather: is effect of sunburn admitted?

indicators.note: the breather word lets the other pieces in, holding them inside itself

parts.note: a rest is a breather, a short pause
taken as written
a tan is what the sun leaves on skin

explanation.surface: A sunbather refuses to lie down for a rest, wondering whether sunburn has been let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' is the container signal: the breather word takes the other two pieces inside it, and 'for' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will not lie down and take it is defiant, opposing what is done to them.

clue.text: Professorship in church music?

parts.note: an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: Asks whether there is a professorship of church music.
explanation.definitionFit: A university's senior professorial post is called a chair, as in holding the chair of history.

clue.text: Church feature of a longer variety

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means they are rearranged into a different form

explanation.surface: A church feature that comes in a longer version.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel roof is a medieval timber church ceiling decorated with carved angels.

clue.text: Conductor has been a figure of fun, we hear

indicators.note: this tells us the word is taken as spoken, matching another spelling

parts.words: has been a figure of fun
parts.note: to be guyed is to be mocked or made a figure of fun

explanation.surface: A conductor has been laughed at, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide leads people around, as a tour conductor does.

clue.text: Cause of structural change in relation to a good fellow

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
a gent is a gentleman, a decent chap

explanation.surface: A good friend causes a change in the structure of a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: In chemistry a reagent is a substance added to cause a reaction, changing molecular structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical reagent is added to bring about a reaction that transforms substances.

clue.text: Permit to follow a Greek character requires charm

indicators.note: the permit word comes after the Greek letter piece

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Permission to trail a Greek figure demands charm.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a trinket worn as a talisman against harm.

clue.text: Test for cars or car

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles, named after the Ministry of Transport

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is a test for cars or a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is an everyday British word for an automobile.

clue.text: Utopia to be suspended in part of Ceylon

indicators.note: the suspended piece goes inside the shortened island name
only some of the country's name is used, losing its final letters

parts.note: Ceylon is the old name of Sri Lanka
to hang is to be suspended

explanation.surface: Paradise is found hanging in a corner of Ceylon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' cuts SRI LANKA to SRILA; HANG goes in after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the hidden paradise of James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, an ideal place.

clue.text: Abhors article, and also is upset about it

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the article
being upset means the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone abhors a certain item and is upset by it too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is upset' scrambles the word 'also', and 'about' wraps that scramble round the article; 'and' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest, so one who loathes abhors.

clue.text: Make easy — to experience again is without point

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the experience word surrounds the point

parts.note: to relive is to go through again
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Making things easy means living through it again without any point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; E goes in RELIVE before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain or a burden is to ease it.

clue.text: The painter I forsake was a giant

indicators.note: forsaking the letter means leaving it out of the painter's name

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits abandoning a painter who was a giant of art.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant deities of Greek myth, so the word means a colossus.

clue.text: FDR was another with the cards

definitions.meaning: Franklin D Roosevelt was the champion of his 1930s recovery programme, a supporter of that deal
a fresh person to deal the playing cards

explanation.surface: President Roosevelt took his turn handing out the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's Depression policy was the New Deal, whose supporters bore that name; also a fresh person who deals cards.

clue.text: Spaceman of a sort-nothing reported

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Spaceman of a sort-nothing reported (9)': ASTRO must come from rearranging 'a sort', but the only anagram signal is 'sort' itself, so 'sort' would do two jobs.

clue.text: Sailor boy in a sheet

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
Paul is a boy's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young seaman wrapped in a sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarpaulin itself was once slang for a sailor, which reinforces the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a large waterproof covering cloth.

clue.text: Oxford man (not at Oriel) provides critic of a text

indicators.note: the words supply the answer from within their own letters running across them

explanation.surface: An Oxford man who is not at Oriel College turns out to be a literary critic.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is an Oxford college; ignore the brackets and read straight through 'man not at Oriel'.
explanation.definitionFit: An annotator writes notes and commentary on a text.

clue.text: Eat words-a strange way to make a splash

indicators.note: putting the letters in a strange way means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Eating one's words is a peculiar way to cause a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link; a splash of soda is the small drop added to a whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash in a drink is a small dash of fizzy mixer.

clue.text: Home Counties prize leaving the land?

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
an award is a prize

explanation.surface: A prize in the Home Counties goes to someone moving out of the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the ocean means departing from the shore, so the direction is away from dry ground.

clue.text: Receiver round field?

definitions.meaning: a dealer in stolen goods, a receiver in criminal slang

explanation.surface: Asks whether a receiver goes round a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is criminal slang for a buyer of stolen goods, and also an enclosing barrier.

clue.text: In time the deserter will make mistakes

indicators.note: the deserter is placed in the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Eventually the runaway soldier will make errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are printing errors listed for correction.

clue.text: Fruit for she yaks, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Fruit for female yaks, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash keys are the winged seeds of the ash tree, botanically its fruit.

clue.text: Runners out of form?

definitions.meaning: an animal that has left its form, the shallow hollow where it lies

explanation.surface: Athletes who are off their form.
explanation.definitionFit: Hares are swift runners, and a hare's lair is called a form.

clue.text: A blow to much of Ulster's government?

indicators.note: only the greater part of the name is used, the end dropped

parts.note: Stormont is the seat of the Northern Ireland government

explanation.surface: A setback for most of Northern Ireland's administration.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a gale, a violent wind.

clue.text: Such a cast is great for the table — quids in!

indicators.note: the money goes inside the table word

parts.note: the altar is the communion table in a church
quid is slang for a pound, and L for libra is the pound sign, so pounds are Ls

explanation.surface: A cast of big names is great for the box office, making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quids in' is British slang for being in profit, and here 'in' puts the pounds inside the table word.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast is one made entirely of famous performers.

clue.text: Having little weight it goes at great speed

definitions.meaning: the radiation that travels fastest of anything

explanation.surface: Something weightless that moves very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Light means not heavy, and light itself travels at the universe's top speed.

clue.text: Gull of 1.4

parts.note: 1.4 is the British way of writing the first of the fourth month; a gull is a dupe tricked on that day

explanation.surface: A seabird of some numbered kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tricked by a prank on the first day of the fourth month is the victim of that day's hoaxes.

clue.text: Creature keeping time was nobbled

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the creature contains the time letter

parts.note: a goat is a creature

explanation.surface: An animal that kept time had been tampered with.
explanation.walkthrough: To nobble, in British slang, is to tamper with or bribe, especially a racehorse or juror.
explanation.definitionFit: To get at someone is to bribe or tamper with them, as nobbled implies.

clue.text: Sir, my indicator could be biased — or not

indicators.note: signals the letters could be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: A man wonders if his indicator is biased.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or not' admits the older sense, discerning or discriminating with good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair treatment of groups is prejudiced, while discerning judgement also distinguishes, hence the double sense.
